name: MD-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 10 points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Johnny Olszewski has a massive fundraising edge ($1.04M raised vs $20K)
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 94%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Olszewski: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a roughly 50-to-1 fundraising advantage over Dave Wallace, with markets agreeing at about 94% for the Democrat. With no polls to contradict that picture, the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin of about 21 points.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race, or a major shift in the national House environment toward Republicans, would be the main reason to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 2nd District sits in the Baltimore suburbs and leans Democratic by about 10 points on the partisan baseline. First-term incumbent Johnny Olszewski is running for reelection and holds a decisive financial advantage, having raised over $1 million and reporting more than $600,000 on hand. Republican Dave Wallace has raised only about $20,000, leaving him little capacity to compete, and no outside spending has materialized on either side.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at roughly 94%. The combination points to a comfortable incumbent win, with the usual caveat that uncertainty is elevated in the absence of polling.
